what_happened: Job 20261028-082300-y4yj ("Require a code survey in readings with new outputs or behavior tests") failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 2 of 3 the critic said the plan was sound and grounded in real code. It still rejected the job because the accepted reading missed a direct consequence of the change. The new rule in check_reading_acceptance would refuse stored change/code readings that have a behavior criterion. The replay that runs on every job would therefore hold the job, and a held replay fails the verdict. None of the reading's six criteria says a higher refusal rate is intended, and the replay only accepts that if a criterion uses an INTENDED_REFUSAL_PHRASES phrase. The critic gave one blocker (no intended-refusal criterion, so the producer stops at step 1) and two minor findings: signal C fires on any mention of records/, and one keyword is enough to satisfy the evidence rule. It also gave one nit about `git diff --stat`. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The reader writes criteria from the request's wording and does not trace the pipeline's own gates that every job passes through. The replay gate runs on every job and holds any job that raises the refusal rate unless a criterion declares the rise intended. Nothing in the reader brief or in reading acceptance tells the reader about that coupling, so a reading for a new refusal rule is accepted without the criterion. Only the planning critic, which reads run/mod.rs and reading.rs, finds the gap, and it finds it after planning spend. The planner cannot repair a reading gap, so the job dies there.
prevention: Add a check at reading acceptance. When a reading's deliverables touch the reading-refusal rules (check_reading_acceptance or the refusal rule list), it must contain at least one criterion that uses an INTENDED_REFUSAL_PHRASES phrase, or the reading is refused with a message naming the missing criterion. Add a line about this to the reader brief so the reader writes the criterion at the first attempt. The same check can run the replay dry against the proposed rule when the reading is built, so the held-job outcome shows up before planning.
proposed_request: Make readings that change the reading-refusal rules declare the intended refusals. Outcome: when an accepted reading's deliverables change check_reading_acceptance or the other reading refusal rules, reading acceptance refuses the reading unless at least one acceptance criterion uses a phrase from INTENDED_REFUSAL_PHRASES, saying that a higher refusal rate of stored readings is intended. The refusal message must name the missing criterion. Add one line to the reader brief telling the reader to include such a criterion whenever a request adds or tightens a refusal rule, and keep the briefs token-budget test passing. Acceptance: (1) a test calls the real check_reading_acceptance with a reading that edits the refusal rules and has no intended-refusal criterion, and it is refused; (2) the same reading with one criterion using an INTENDED_REFUSAL_PHRASES phrase is accepted; (3) a reading that does not touch the refusal rules is unaffected; (4) fmt, clippy and test pass. Do not change the replay itself. Then resubmit "Require a code survey in readings with new outputs or behavior tests" as a follow-up. Its reading must carry over the plan the critic called sound and add an intended-refusal criterion. It must also say that signal C ignores criteria that mention records/ only to exclude it, and that the evidence rule needs more than a passing keyword mention.
